Hi there! I'm putting together a summer backyard barbecue for about 20 friends and family members, and I could use some help planning a menu that works well for both kids and adults.

Prepare large batches of mild burgers and hot dogs to satisfy children. Add grilled corn on the cob and simple potato salad for easy sides. Serve watermelon and classic ice cream for dessert. These options require minimal supervision and appeal to all ages without complex preparation.
Thanks for those ideas! How much food should I plan on per person if I'm offering a couple of main meat options plus sides and dessert?

Plan for two burgers or three hot dogs per adult and one or two per child. Allocate half a pound of each main meat per person to account for varied appetites. Provide one cup of each side dish per guest and ensure ample dessert portions. This quantity prevents waste while ensuring everyone leaves satisfied.

Serve plain grilled chicken burgers, hot dogs, and corn on the cob. Keep sauces and seasonings on the side so adults can customize their meals while kids stick to simple options. Add watermelon slices and potato salad for easy, crowd-pleasing sides that require minimal preparation.
That sounds like a solid mix, thanks — how much food should I plan per person if I'm doing a couple of main options and several sides?

Plan for two protein items per person, such as one burger or hot dog plus a small portion of grilled chicken. Allocate roughly one cup of each side dish per guest to account for varying appetites. Prepare ten percent extra food to cover unexpected hunger or larger portions without significant waste.
Hi there! I'm putting together a backyard barbecue for about 25 friends and family this summer, and I could really use some menu ideas that work well for both kids and adults.

Grilled chicken skewers and veggie burgers are great crowd-pleasers that appeal to all ages. Add classic sides like corn on the cob and potato salad to keep things simple and satisfying. Finish with fruit skewers and watermelon slices for a refreshing, kid-friendly dessert option that everyone will enjoy.
That sounds like a great mix — how should I estimate the quantities of meat and sides per person so I don't run short?

Plan for about six to eight ounces of meat per adult and four to six ounces for children to ensure everyone gets enough. For sides, aim for one cup per person for heavier items like potato salad and half a cup for lighter options such as corn. Always prepare slightly more than your exact calculations since guests often eat more than expected at outdoor gatherings.
